tools.title: BIM2AR
tools.description: IFC models in 3D and augmented reality, with IFC-linked site inspection, entirely in the browser. Open a building model on a phone, tablet or computer, inspect it in 3D, place it on a table or at full scale in AR, and record what you find on site, with every record tied to the IFC element's GlobalId.

sections.title: From IFC Model to Site Verification
paragraphs: BIM2AR opens an IFC building model (IFC2x3 or IFC4) on a phone, tablet or computer. You inspect it in 3D, place it on a table or at full scale in augmented reality, and record what you find on site. Every inspection record, note and photo is tied to the IFC element's GlobalId, so records survive a re-exported model and can be traced back to the element they describe.

Four modes share one model, one set of element identifiers, the same BIM layers and the same inspection data: 3D Viewer for exploring the model, AR Viewer for seeing it in the room, AR Pro for sections, measurements, annotations and captures, and AR Verify for checking the building against the model with reference-point site calibration and per-element verification status. Switching mode never reloads the file.

Nothing is uploaded. IFC files, notes, inspection records and photos stay on the device unless you export them, and there is no server, account or database. IFC parsing runs in a Web Worker with web-ifc (WASM), AR uses WebXR on ARCore-capable Android devices, and iPhone and iPad users get an AR Quick Look (USDZ) fallback.

items.html: 3D viewer: spatial tree, IFC classes and schema browser, element search by name, class, GlobalId or Property:value, properties, storey filter and saved views

BIM layers: Architecture, Structure, Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, Spaces, Envelope and Furniture, classified from IfcSystem membership, property sets and IFC class, with the reason shown for each element
WebXR AR: tabletop (1:200 to 1:20), full-scale 1:1 or component placement, with hit-test surface placement, spatial anchors and world locking
AR Pro: horizontal and vertical section planes and a section box, rendering modes, model and AR measurements, categorised annotations and image markup
Site calibration: reference-point alignment with RMS and maximum residuals, leave-one-out error and a plan-scale check
AR Verify: per-element status (verified, discrepancy, missing, obstructed, follow up), discrepancy types, observed positions and evidence photos
Reports and packages: inspection reports as PDF, HTML, JSON or CSV, and portable .bim2ar.zip project packages
Mobile first: layouts for phone, tablet and desktop in portrait or landscape, left or right-handed controls, and autosave on the device

tools.title: Parametra
tools.description: House designs shaped around how you live. Describe a plot, a household and a style, and Parametra lays out dozens of complete house designs, scores each one against your priorities, and lets you explore the best four as dimensioned floor plans and as a furnished 3D model, with IFC4 BIM export.

sections.title: From Brief to Buildable Concept
paragraphs: Parametra turns a short brief into complete house designs. Describe your plot, your household and the style you like, and it lays out dozens of designs, scores each one against your priorities, and lets you explore the best four as dimensioned floor plans and as a furnished 3D model with landscaping. It is free to use in the browser, with no account and nothing to install.

Each brief explores 36–108 layout variants. The brief becomes a room program (suites, kitchen with pantry, laundry with store), rooms are assigned to floors, and every storey is laid out in a street band, a 1.2 m circulation spine and a garden band with a stair aligned on every level. Walls, doors, windows and furniture are then derived, and each design is scored on nine criteria weighted by your priority sliders: efficiency, proportions, daylight, solar orientation, functional flow, privacy, area match, site fit and build economy.

It is a fully static site written in plain HTML, CSS and ES modules, with no build step and no backend. Three.js is vendored, so the only external request is Google Fonts. Designs are concept-stage studies for briefing an architect, not construction documents, and costs are indicative.

items.html: Guided brief: six steps (plot, size, rooms, kitchen and outdoors, style, priorities) with a live preview of the best layout
Design studio: four recommended designs as tabs, with Overview, Rooms, Scores and Materials details and an estimated build cost
3D viewer: orbit the house, cut away each level with a section plane, or walk through it in first person
Sun-position slider tied to the plot's orientation and hemisphere, camera presets and layer toggles
Dimensioned SVG floor plans for every level, in plan view or side by side with the 3D model
Seven architectural styles, each with its own glazing, materials, tree species and boundary walls or fences
Procedural landscaping: shader lawn with 3D grass, branching trees with dappled shadows, shrubs and planted beds
Exports: IFC4 BIM model (passes IfcOpenShell validation), GLB scene, SVG plans, PNG render and JSON design data

tools.title: BIM2Bot Lab
tools.description: From IFC model to robot route, entirely in the browser. A free construction informatics lab that explores IFC models, turns them into maps a robot can plan on, compares routes, exports ROS 2 (Nav2) maps, and simulates robot fleets with simulated LiDAR, lifts, door schedules and people moving through the building.

sections.title: IFC to Robot Route in the Browser
paragraphs: BIM2Bot Lab is a free construction informatics lab that runs in the browser. Open an IFC model to explore its geometry and semantics, turn it into maps a robot can plan on, and simulate robot fleets moving through the building. Every navigation result can be traced back to the IFC elements and processing steps that produced it.

Nothing is uploaded: IFC2x3, IFC4 and IFC4.3 files are parsed on your device with web-ifc (WebAssembly). A room graph (S1–S5) links storeys, rooms, doors, stairs, ramps and lifts, while occupancy grids (G1–G6) rasterise floors and obstacles, carve doors, apply safety zones, inflate for the robot's size, and run multi-level A* path search. Each map cell and graph edge records the IFC element that produced it.

Routes can be compared by distance, time and energy, and exported as ROS 2 Nav2 maps (PGM + YAML per level) with FollowWaypoints goals. In the simulation, every robot has its own 3D model and a simulated 2D LiDAR; doors can close and reopen on a schedule, and batch experiments sweep parameters across seeds.

items.html: Explore: 3D and 2D IFC viewer with model browser, IFC schema browser, inspector, search, and model checks
Navigate: occupancy grids and a room graph derived from IFC, with multi-level A* routes
Configurable robot profiles: width, height, clearance, and stair or lift use
What-if analysis with user-placed obstacles, blocked doors, lifts added to stair cores, and no-go or slow safety zones
Cell-level traceability: see which IFC element and pipeline step made a cell free, blocked, or too narrow
Route comparison by distance, estimated time and energy (fewest level changes, no lifts, no stairs)
ROS 2 export: Nav2 map_server maps (PGM + YAML) per level, plus route waypoints and FollowWaypoints goals
Simulate: deterministic, seeded fleets with lift scheduling, congestion handling, door schedules with re-planning, and human–robot interaction
3D robot models per profile (wheeled, compact, quadruped, hospital cart), each with a simulated 2D LiDAR exported as LaserScan JSON
Results with makespan, throughput, congestion heatmaps, lift waits, batch experiments across seeds, and JSON/CSV export
Privacy by design: files stay on your device, hosted as a static site on GitHub Pages

tools.title: BIM2BEM
tools.description: From IFC model to building energy model, entirely in the browser. BIM2BEM converts an IFC model into an EnergyPlus model, runs EnergyPlus (WebAssembly) in the page with weather for the building's real location, and evaluates energy demand and indoor environmental quality. Every input says where it came from.

sections.title: IFC to EnergyPlus in the Browser
paragraphs: BIM2BEM converts an IFC building model into an EnergyPlus model, runs EnergyPlus 26.2 compiled to WebAssembly in the page with weather data for the building's real location, and evaluates energy demand and indoor environmental quality. It is a static site: no server, no account, no upload. IFC files are parsed and simulated on your machine.

Every number shown says where it came from: the IFC file, IFC geometry (calculated), your entries, an open dataset, a documented reference library, or a reconstruction by the conversion algorithm. Where an analysis cannot be calculated from the available inputs, the app says so instead of showing a value.

BIM2BEM grew out of BIM2Bot Lab: the IFC loading, 3D viewer, model tree, property inspection and 2D floor plans are kept, while the robot navigation and simulation features are replaced by an energy-modelling workflow.

items.html: Location: reads IfcSite coordinates and true north for you to confirm, or search an address, pick on the map or type coordinates
Weather fetched automatically: a nearby TMY3 file, otherwise the latest complete year from Open-Meteo (ERA5) or NASA POWER; or upload your own validated EPW
IFC → BEM conversion: IfcSpace to thermal zones and surfaces from second-level space boundaries where complete, otherwise reconstructed from space bodies
Constructions from IFC material layers and thermal properties, declared U-values, or documented reference constructions; never inferred from a material's name
Energy simulation: IDF validated against the engine schema, EnergyPlus run in a Web Worker, with scenarios for insulation, glazing, ventilation and setpoints
IEQ analysis: PMV/PPD (ISO 7730), adaptive comfort (EN 16798-1, ASHRAE 55), CO₂, outdoor-air rates and daylight per zone
Environment: wind rose, sun path, monthly radiation and incident solar radiation on exterior surfaces
Traceability: every IFC element lists the zones, surfaces and openings it produced, exported as JSON and CSV with GlobalIds
Exports: IDF, epJSON, IFC→BEM mapping, zone and hourly results, assumptions, a reproducibility manifest and a printable report

tools.title: BIM2REUSE

logo.alt: BIM2REUSE: From BIM to Circular Construction

tools.description: From BIM to circular construction, entirely in the browser. BIM2REUSE turns a building, with or without a BIM model, into traceable material reuse decisions: what it is made of, which components could be reused, how they come out, where they could go in a new building, and what that saves in carbon and cost.

sections.title: Circular Construction in the Browser
paragraphs: BIM2REUSE is a free, open-source web application for circular construction. Open the IFC model of an existing building, or survey a building that has no model, and it builds the information that reuse decisions need, from the material inventory and material passports to a deconstruction plan, a material bank, an optimal reuse allocation and a carbon and cost comparison.

Every record stays linked to the component it describes: the IFC GlobalId of a model element, or the persistent component ID of a surveyed one. Every value records where it came from (IFC, geometry, drawings, an imported file, a manual entry, an estimate or a verified inspection), and missing values stay missing instead of being guessed.

Private by design: there is no server. IFC files are read on your device with web-ifc (WebAssembly), and projects, documents and photographs are saved in your browser. Nothing you open or enter is uploaded.

items.html: Explore: open an IFC2x3, IFC4 or IFC4.3 model in the IFC Viewer, or record a building without BIM in Building Survey
Inventory: materials, volumes and masses of every element, with the source of each value
Document: a material passport for each component, pre-filled from the model
Assess: mandatory checks plus a weighted screening index for each component's reuse pathway
Plan: deconstruction stages from a dependency graph of removal tasks
Bank: a catalogue of recoverable components from one or more buildings
Match: an optimal allocation of banked components to a new building, with cutting plans (HiGHS mixed-integer solver)
Compare: carbon and cost of building new versus building with reused components
Report: one technical report, printable to PDF, and a portable project package

tools.title: ReUniXchange
tools.description: Data exchange platform for BIM interoperability and standardized information sharing across AEC workflows.

sections.title: Data Exchange Platform
paragraphs: ReUniXchange is a cutting-edge Revit plugin that enables seamless export of BIM geometry, metadata, and materials to Unity. It supports modular construction workflows and immersive XR applications by bridging the gap between design and visualization environments. The plugin allows users to assign shared parameters (ModularID) to Revit group components, extract structured metadata into CSV format, export 3D views as OBJ files with MTL and texture data, and re-import any changes made in Unity through an XML file.

For modular projects, the plugin can automatically generate ModularID parameters based on group names, enabling logical tracking and reconstruction of elements inside Unity. Metadata from Revit views can be exported to CSV and attached to 3D objects inside Unity to enable semantic enrichment, selection, and inspection during runtime. Material definitions used in Revit are also exported into Unity-readable MTL files with associated texture images.

tools.title: BIM2KnowledgeGraph
tools.description: From IFC model to a traceable knowledge graph, entirely in your browser. BIM2KnowledgeGraph (BIM2KG) reads an IFC model and builds a semantic knowledge graph you can trace back to the file, query with SPARQL or plain-language questions, validate with SHACL, explore next to the 3D model, and export as RDF or as a property graph.

sections.title: IFC to Traceable Knowledge Graphs
paragraphs: BIM2KnowledgeGraph reads an IFC model (IFC2x3, IFC4 or IFC4x3, as .ifc or .ifczip) and builds a knowledge graph you can trace back to the file. Every node keeps its GlobalId and STEP id, and every relationship names the IFC relationship it came from.

Everything the tool derives (hosting, MEP flow, space adjacency, access, geometric contact, robot accessibility) records its rule, parameters and verification state, separately from what the file states. IFC files are processed in the browser and never uploaded.
Using Revit or ArchiCAD? Export an IFC file from the authoring tool and open it in the app.

items.html: Parsing & identity: streaming ISO 10303-21 parser, SHA-256 fingerprint of the source and GlobalId-based IRIs scoped to the file
Semantic model: every IfcRel* as a typed edge, with property and quantity sets, units, materials, classifications, ports, systems, zones and tasks
Enrichment rules with provenance: hosting, MEP flow, space adjacency, door / stair / lift access, geometric contact and robot-navigation accessibility
Graph profiles from full fidelity to simplified, spatial, MEP, material, construction-process, digital-twin and robot-navigation views
Ontologies: BOT, ifcOWL class alignment, LBD PROPS, QUDT and PROV-O, plus optional BEO, Brick, SOSA/SSN, GeoSPARQL and SAREF4BLDG
Query: SPARQL editor with templates, and rule-based plain-language questions (no external AI service)
Validation: up to 26 IFC information-quality checks, SHACL shapes and RDF round-trip of every format
Synchronised 3D viewer: selecting a node highlights its products, and picking a product selects its node
Export: Turtle, JSON-LD, TriG, N-Quads, RDF/XML, GraphML, GEXF, CSV, Neo4j Cypher, ML datasets and SVG / PNG figures

paragraphs: BIMUniXchange is a full AEC-to-XR workflow suite that enables seamless transfer of BIM models from Autodesk Revit and GRAPHISOFT ArchiCAD into Unity for immersive extended reality applications. The pipeline has been tested with 4,000+ building elements, maintaining interactive frame rates in XR on platforms including Meta Quest 3, Samsung S22 Ultra, and desktop VR headsets.

paragraphs: BIM-VR for 4D Simulation is a Unity-based prototype for visualizing modular building manufacturing in an immersive virtual environment. The workflow begins with detailed Autodesk Revit BIM models of a modular house, factory environment, and supporting equipment, then exports geometry and metadata through the custom ReUniXchange pipeline.

Inside Unity, OBJ geometry, BIM metadata CSV files, and construction schedule CSV data are mapped to BIM components. The resulting scene supports phase-based animation, real-time schedule control, semantic metadata inspection, desktop navigation, and OpenXR-compatible VR deployment.

sections.title: IFC ↔ OpenUSD, Without Losing the BIM
paragraphs: IfcUSD is a Python package and command-line tool for researchers and practitioners who need building models in NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, Unity or any OpenUSD pipeline, with their building information. It reads every IFC version through IfcOpenShell, writes OpenUSD through Pixar's usd-core, and proves that nothing was lost: a coverage report accounts for every IfcRoot instance (missing: 0).

Geometry, spatial structure, every attribute, property and quantity, types, materials, classifications, groups and relationships are written as typed, documented USD data using a versioned, codeless USD schema (IfcEntityAPI, IfcPropertySetAPI, IfcQuantitySetAPI, …). Output goes to .usd, .usda, .usdc or .usdz, together with report.json and metadata.json.

It also works in the other direction. ifcusd to-ifc writes USD back to IFC, either into the original file (only what changed) or as a model rebuilt from USD. Robots, sensors and obstacles become IFC elements, and physics, trajectories, sensor time series and semantic labels become property sets, time series and classifications, declared as property set templates inside the file.

items.html: Complete: all attributes, every property kind, quantities with units, types, material sets, classifications, documents, groups, systems, zones and all IfcRel* relationships
Typed and reversible: values keep their IFC types, defined types and units; original names kept in displayName
Any IFC version: IFC2X3, IFC4 and IFC4X3 natively, IFC5 (.ifcx) with layer composition, and .ifczip
Accurate geometry: local meshes under double-precision transforms, instancing, per-face materials, axes and alignments as curves; verified against IfcOpenShell to 5 × 10⁻⁵ m
Reproducible: byte-identical output for any thread count, with provenance (source SHA-256, versions, options) in every file
Target profiles: NVIDIA Omniverse (OmniPBR, Replicator semantic labels), Unity 6 (Y-up, metadata sidecar plus editor script) and generic OpenUSD
Both directions: ifcusd to-ifc returns robot and simulation results to IFC using only standard IFC mechanisms

sections.title: Install & Quick Start
paragraphs: Python 3.10 – 3.14 on Windows, macOS or Linux. The dependencies (ifcopenshell, usd-core, numpy) install automatically as binary wheels. See the documentation for the tutorial, IFC ↔ USD mapping and API reference.
sections.code:
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/isaddiq/ifcusd.git"

ifcusd convert model.ifc model.usdc                          # any OpenUSD tool
ifcusd convert model.ifc model.usdc --profile omniverse      # NVIDIA Omniverse
ifcusd convert model.ifc model.usdz --profile unity --metadata-json model.ifcusd.json
ifcusd convert model.ifc model.usdc --validate --report report.json
ifcusd to-ifc model.usdc model.trained.ifc --source model.ifc --layer robot_run.usda --validate
ifcusd ui                                                    # IfcUSD Studio in the browser

tools.title: Kyung Hee University Global Campus: 3D Digital Twin
tools.description: An interactive, geographically referenced 3D reconstruction of Kyung Hee University Global Campus in Yongin, built on CesiumJS. Real terrain at 1:1 scale, 41 campus buildings on their OpenStreetMap footprints, first-person walking and GLB export, with every estimated or stylised value labelled.

sections.title: Geospatial 3D Digital Twin of the Campus
paragraphs: An interactive, geographically referenced 3D reconstruction of Kyung Hee University Global Campus (경희대학교 국제캠퍼스, 1732 Deogyeong-daero, Giheung-gu, Yongin-si). It is a static website built on CesiumJS: no server, build step or API key is needed.

Its priorities are geographic correctness first, completeness second and visual realism third. Every geometric value in the scene comes from a real dataset (FABDEM bare-earth terrain, Copernicus DEM, OpenStreetMap and the official KHU campus map), and every value that is estimated or stylised is labelled as such in the interface and in a machine-readable accuracy report.

It is made for education and research, as an open, reproducible starting point for a campus digital twin: teaching geospatial methods, adding indoor plans and sensor feeds, or studying sunlight, routes, stormwater and evacuation on the real slopes. Use is non-commercial, and it is an independent reconstruction, not an official Kyung Hee University product.

items.html: Real terrain at 1:1 scale: FABDEM V1-2 bare-earth DTM, EGM2008 geoid applied, in realistic, elevation, slope, contour and wireframe modes
41 campus buildings on their real OSM footprints (1,104 with the ~600 m context ring); 24/24 official campus-map entries matched
Special models for the main gate (정문), the 평화노천극장 amphitheatre with 41 terraces cut from the DTM, and the 천문대 observatory
Roads, footways, steps, parking, landcover and POIs draped on the terrain, with vegetation from OSM woods and a canopy-height model
Navigation: orbit, fly-through, top-down and first-person walk at 1.7 m eye height, with building collisions and a touch movement pad
Building information: Korean/English names, campus-map number, OSM id, WGS84 and EPSG:5186 coordinates, height with its documented/derived/estimated status
Sun position and time of day with shadows, and a Data & accuracy dialog
Export GLB: the whole campus as one glTF file with every building, surface and tree as its own named node

sections.title: Run Locally
paragraphs: Use the live app, or serve the web/ folder locally. To rebuild the data from source, run the Python pipeline:
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/isaddiq/KyungHeeUniversity_GlobalCampus.git
cd KyungHeeUniversity_GlobalCampus
python -m http.server 8000 --directory web   # open http://localhost:8000/

pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/run_all.py                    # rebuild web/data from source
